people: Preston Martin (Vice Chair, Board of Governors, March 31, 1982 to April 30, 1986)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that before joining the Board, Preston Martin was a professor of finance at the University of Southern California from 1959 to 1963, worked in homebuilding, shopping center development and the organizing of banks, mortgage finance and savings and loan businesses, served as California savings and loan commissioner from 1969, and chaired the Federal Home Loan Bank Board from 1969 to 1972. He was Vice Chair of the Board of Governors from March 31, 1982 and resigned effective April 30, 1986. The page states that after the Fed he founded PMI Mortgage Insurance Co. and later Seraco Enterprises, Inc., a subsidiary of Sears Roebuck, sat on the board of directors of Sears and several other companies, and entered a partnership with former Treasury Secretary William Simon that took control of failing thrifts and banks. No dates are given for the post-Fed roles. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from private banking and savings-and-loan ventures to the Fed vice chairmanship, and from there to founding PMI Mortgage Insurance Co. and a partnership taking over failing thrifts and banks

people: Manuel H. Johnson (Governor from February 7, 1986; Vice Chair from August 22, 1986; left August 3, 1990)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Manuel H. Johnson was a deputy assistant secretary at the Treasury Department from 1981 to 1982 and assistant secretary from 1982 to 1986, and a professor of economics at George Mason University from 1977 to 1994. He was sworn in as a Governor on February 7, 1986, appointed Vice Chair on August 22, 1986, and left the Board on August 3, 1990. The page states that from 1990 he was cochairman and senior partner of Johnson Smick International, Inc., which it describes as an investment and consulting firm. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the Treasury to the Fed vice chairmanship, and from there to Johnson Smick International, Inc., an investment and consulting firm

people: David W. Mullins Jr. (Governor from May 21, 1990; Vice Chair from July 24, 1991; resigned effective February 14, 1994)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that David W. Mullins Jr. was on the finance faculty of Harvard Business School from 1974 to 1988 and then assistant secretary for domestic finance at the US Department of the Treasury from 1988. He became a Governor on May 21, 1990 and Vice Chair on July 24, 1991, and his resignation took effect February 14, 1994. The page states that he left the Board in 1994 to join Long-Term Capital Management, which it describes as an investment firm, and names no other post-Fed employer. No ethics finding is recorded.
source_title: David W. Mullins Jr. (Federal Reserve History)
move: from the Treasury to the Fed vice chairmanship, and from there to the investment firm Long-Term Capital Management

people: Martha R. Seger (Governor, Board of Governors, July 2, 1984 to March 3, 1991)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Martha R. Seger accepted a post as a financial economist at the Board of Governors in 1964, became chief economist at Detroit Bank and Trust about three years later, and in 1974 became vice president in charge of economics and investments at the Bank of the Commonwealth in Detroit. She sat on the board of Michigan Blue Cross/Blue Shield from 1974 to 1976, taught from 1976 to 1984, and was Michigan's Commissioner of Financial Institutions from 1981 to 1982. She served as a Governor from July 2, 1984 to March 3, 1991. The page states that from 1994 to 2001 she was principal and economic consultant at M.R. Seger & Associates, a financial and economic consulting firm, and that she sat on the boards of Amerisure Companies, Xerox Corp., Kroger Co., Johnson Controls Inc. and Amoco Co., with no dates given. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from Detroit Bank and Trust and the Bank of the Commonwealth to a Fed governorship, and from there to her own firm M.R. Seger & Associates

people: John P. LaWare (Governor, Board of Governors, August 15, 1988 to April 30, 1995)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that John P. LaWare began a career in finance in 1953, rose through the ranks at Chemical Bank & Trust Co. in New York, and later worked at Shawmut Bank in Boston, where he served as a Federal Advisory Council member from 1986 to 1988 and as a director of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston in 1988. He was a Governor from August 15, 1988 until his resignation on April 30, 1995. The page states that after retiring from the Board in 1995 he became an advisory director of Stewart Information Services Corp., and that he was a director of Liberty Mutual Insurance Company and a trustee of Travelers Real Estate Investors Trust, with no dates given. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from Chemical Bank & Trust and Shawmut Bank to a Fed governorship, and from there to Stewart Information Services Corp.

people: H. Robert Heller (Governor, Board of Governors, August 19, 1986 to July 31, 1989)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that H. Robert Heller taught economics at UCLA from 1965 to 1971 and later at the University of Hawaii, was chief of the financial studies division at the International Monetary Fund from 1974, and from 1978 was senior vice president and director of international economic research at Bank of America in San Francisco. He was a Governor from August 19, 1986 to July 31, 1989. The page states that after leaving the Board he joined Visa, was president and chief executive officer of Visa U.S.A. from 1991 for two years, and was executive vice president of Fair Isaac Corporation from 1994 to 2001. It also lists current board seats at Bank of Marin and Bank of Marin Bancorp and at Sonic Automotive, Inc., and a past seat at BMW of North America. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from Bank of America to a Fed governorship, and from there to Visa U.S.A. as chief executive and then Fair Isaac Corporation

people: Wayne D. Angell (Governor, Board of Governors, sworn in February 7, 1986; retired February 2, 1994)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Wayne D. Angell was a professor and later chair of economics at Ottawa University in Kansas from 1956 to 1985, served in the Kansas House of Representatives from 1960 to 1966, and was an officer and director of several banks in Kansas and Missouri from 1971 to 1985; the page does not name those banks. He was sworn in as a Governor on February 7, 1986, filling Lyle E. Gramley's unexpired term, and retired February 2, 1994. The page states that upon retiring from the Board in 1994 he became chief economist at Bear Stearns & Co., Inc. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from bank officer and director roles in Kansas and Missouri to a Fed governorship, and from there to chief economist at Bear Stearns

people: Susan M. Phillips (Governor, Board of Governors, sworn in December 2, 1991; left June 20, 1998)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Susan M. Phillips taught at Louisiana State University and was an assistant professor of business administration at the University of Iowa in 1974, was a Brookings economic policy fellow from 1976 to 1977 and an economic fellow at the Securities and Exchange Commission the following year, held senior administrative posts at the University of Iowa from 1978, was appointed to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in 1981, chaired it from 1983, was reappointed in 1985 and resigned in 1987, then returned to the University of Iowa as vice president. She was a Governor from December 2, 1991 to June 20, 1998. The page states that she then became dean of the business school at George Washington University, retiring as dean in 2010, and lists current board seats at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Chicago Futures Exchange, Kroger and State Farm Insurance, with no dates given. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the CFTC chairmanship to a Fed governorship, and from there to board seats at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Chicago Futures Exchange and State Farm Insurance

people: Edward W. Kelley Jr. (Governor, Board of Governors, sworn in May 26, 1987; reappointed April 20, 1990; retired December 31, 2001)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Edward W. Kelley Jr. returned to Houston after earning his MBA in 1959 to become president of Kelley Manufacturing Company, the firm his father established in 1937, and expanded it into a holding company. The page states that he sold his company in 1981 and became chairman of Investment Advisors, Inc. that same year. He was sworn in as a Governor on May 26, 1987, reappointed and sworn in for a second term on April 20, 1990, and retired December 31, 2001. The page lists him as a founding director of Southern National Bank, Westwood Commerce Bank and West Belt National Bank, a director of Promontory Interfinancial Network, LLC, and a trustee of the Financial Accounting Foundation Inc., without stating whether these roles came before or after his Fed service. It names no employer after 2001. No ethics finding is recorded.
source_title: Edward W. Kelley Jr. (Federal Reserve History)
move: from the chairmanship of Investment Advisors, Inc. to a Fed governorship, with founding directorships at Southern National Bank, Westwood Commerce Bank and West Belt National Bank and a directorship at Promontory Interfinancial Network

people: Emmett J. Rice (Governor, Board of Governors, June 20, 1979 to December 31, 1986)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Emmett J. Rice taught economics at the University of California, Berkeley and at Cornell University, was a research associate at India's central bank in the early 1950s on a Fulbright fellowship, was an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York during a 1960 sabbatical, helped establish the Central Bank of Nigeria from 1962, was deputy and then acting director of the Treasury Department's Office of the Developing Nations from 1964, and was appointed alternate US director at the World Bank in 1966. The page states that he joined The National Bank of Washington in 1972 and rose to senior vice president. He was appointed to the Board by President Jimmy Carter in April 1979 and served from June 20, 1979 to December 31, 1986. The page names no private employer after his Fed service, listing only civic board seats. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from senior vice president at The National Bank of Washington to a Fed governorship

people: Philip E. Coldwell (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, February 1, 1968 to October 28, 1974; Governor, Board of Governors, October 29, 1974 to February 29, 1980)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Philip E. Coldwell was a combat pilot in the US Navy during World War II and taught economics at the University of Illinois, the University of Montana, the University of Louisiana at Lafayette and the University of Wisconsin. He was an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City in 1951, joined the research department of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas in 1952 and became its director of research about two years later, was president of the Dallas Fed from February 1, 1968 to October 28, 1974, and was a Governor from October 29, 1974 to February 29, 1980. The page states that he then ran Coldwell Financial Consultants in Washington, D.C., giving no start date. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the Dallas Fed presidency and a Fed governorship to Coldwell Financial Consultants

people: J. Charles Partee (Governor, Board of Governors, January 5, 1976 to February 7, 1986)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that J. Charles Partee joined the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago as an economist in 1949, joined Northern Trust Company of Chicago in 1956 as associate economist and was its second vice president from 1958 to 1961, then joined the Board of Governors staff in 1962, holding several roles including managing director for research and economic policy from November 1973. He was a Governor from January 5, 1976 to February 7, 1986. The page states that afterwards he was a board member of State Farm Insurance and a trustee of a family of mutual funds, giving no dates and not naming the funds. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Fed staff and a governorship, and from there to the board of State Farm Insurance and a mutual fund trusteeship

people: Frederick H. Schultz (Vice Chair, Board of Governors, took office July 27, 1979; resigned February 11, 1982)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Frederick H. Schultz served as an artillery officer in Korea from 1952 to 1954, joined Barnett National Bank of Jacksonville in 1956, opened his own firm Schultz Investments in 1957, and was chairman of the board of Barnett Investment Services, Inc. at the time of his Fed appointment, as well as a director of Barnett Banks of Florida and several other major companies the page does not name. He was Vice Chair of the Board of Governors from July 27, 1979 until his resignation on February 11, 1982. The page states that he returned to Florida and continued public service, founding The Schultz Center for Teaching and Leadership in Jacksonville in 1997, and names no post-Fed private employer. He died in 2009. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the chairmanship of Barnett Investment Services and his own Schultz Investments to the Fed vice chairmanship

people: Sherman J. Maisel (Governor, Board of Governors, April 30, 1965 to May 31, 1972)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Sherman J. Maisel was a research economist at the Board of Governors in Washington from 1939 to 1941, served in the US Army from 1941 and reached the rank of captain by 1945, spent a year in the US Foreign Service in Brussels after 1945, and worked at the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley from 1948 until 1965. He was a Governor from April 30, 1965 to May 31, 1972. The page states that he returned to the Haas School from 1972 to 1986, was on the senior research staff of the National Bureau of Economic Research and director of its West Coast office from 1972 to 1980, was chairman of the board of directors of Farmers Savings & Loan from 1986 to 1988, and was president of Sherman J. Maisel & Associates Inc. from 1986 to 2010. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from UC Berkeley to a Fed governorship, and from there to the board chairmanship of Farmers Savings & Loan and his own firm Sherman J. Maisel & Associates

people: J. Dewey Daane (Governor, Board of Governors, November 29, 1963 to March 8, 1974)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that J. Dewey Daane rose from statistician to monetary economist, assistant vice president and vice president in charge of research at the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, was a consultant to an International Monetary Fund fiscal mission to Paraguay from 1950 to 1951, became vice president and economic adviser at the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis in May 1960, and from July 1960 was assistant to the Treasury Secretary for debt management and then deputy undersecretary for monetary affairs. He was appointed to the Board by President Kennedy and served from November 29, 1963 to March 8, 1974. The page states that afterwards he was the Frank K. Houston Professor of Banking at Vanderbilt University, and a senior official including vice chairman of the board at Commerce Union Bank and its successor Sovran Bank in Nashville, with no dates given. It also lists him as a public director of the Chicago Board of Trade from 1979 to 1982, a public director of the National Futures Association from 1987 to 2002, and a director of Whittaker Corporation in Los Angeles from 1974 to 1989. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the Treasury to a Fed governorship, and from there to the vice chairmanship of Commerce Union Bank and its successor Sovran Bank

people: Theodore H. Roberts (President, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, February 1, 1983 to December 31, 1984)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Theodore H. Roberts spent thirty years at Harris Trust and Savings Bank from 1953 to 1983, beginning as a trainee and becoming executive vice president and chief financial officer, and helped found the Association for Modern Banking in Illinois in 1973, later being elected its president. He was president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis from February 1, 1983 to December 31, 1984, succeeding Lawrence K. Roos, and resigned at the end of that period. The page states that he returned to Harris Bank, then became president and chief operating officer of Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan and its chairman and chief executive in 1987, and became president of LaSalle National Bank in 1991 when it purchased Talman, retiring in 1995. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from Harris Trust and Savings Bank to the St. Louis Fed presidency, and from there back to Harris Bank, then Talman Home Federal Savings and Loan and LaSalle National Bank

people: Robert D. McTeer Jr. (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, February 1, 1991 to November 4, 2004)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Robert D. McTeer Jr. earned his bachelor's and doctorate in economics at the University of Georgia and was a professor on its faculty for two years, joined the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond in 1968 as an economist, held management roles there including first vice president, and was named senior vice president of the Richmond Fed's Baltimore branch in 1980. He was the eleventh president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, from February 1, 1991 to November 4, 2004. The page states that after retiring in November 2004 he was chancellor of the Texas A&M University System for two years, was named a Distinguished Fellow of the National Center for Policy Analysis in Dallas in 2007, and holds board seats at Westwood Holdings Group, Beal Bank, Refocus Group and Aquinas Companies, with no dates given. No ethics finding is recorded.
source_title: Robert D. McTeer Jr. (Federal Reserve History)
move: from the Dallas Fed presidency to board seats at Westwood Holdings Group and Beal Bank

people: M. Monroe Kimbrel (President and CEO, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, February 1, 1968 to March 31, 1980)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that M. Monroe Kimbrel worked in the lumber business in Thomson, Georgia and as a credit examiner for the Farm Credit Administration in Columbia, South Carolina, joined the First National Bank of Thomson, Georgia in 1946 and later served as its president and chairman, and was chairman of the Bank of Fort Valley, Georgia. He was a member of the Atlanta Fed's board of directors from 1960 to 1965, became its senior vice president on June 1, 1965 and first vice president about five months later, and was the bank's tenth president and chief executive from February 1, 1968 to March 31, 1980. The page states that after taking early retirement from the Atlanta Fed in 1980 he became vice chairman of the First Railroad and Banking Co. of Georgia. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from the presidency and chairmanship of the First National Bank of Thomson to the Atlanta Fed presidency, and from there to the vice chairmanship of the First Railroad and Banking Co. of Georgia

people: Henry C. Wallich (Governor, Board of Governors, March 8, 1974 to December 15, 1986)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Henry C. Wallich worked in the export business in Argentina and Chile and was a securities analyst in New York City from 1933 to 1940; the page does not name the firm. It states that he joined the staff of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York in 1941 and was chief of its Foreign Research Division from 1946 to 1951, was a professor of economics at Yale University from 1951 to 1970 and the Seymour H. Knox Professor of Economics from 1970 to 1974, was assistant to Treasury Secretary Robert B. Anderson from 1958 to 1959, served on the President's Council of Economic Advisers from 1959 to 1961, and was a senior consultant to the Treasury from 1969 until his Board appointment. He was a Governor from March 8, 1974 until his resignation on December 15, 1986, and died in 1988. The page says he was a former director of a number of business firms but names none and gives no dates. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: from securities analysis in New York City (firm not named) to the New York Fed staff and later a Fed governorship
